column1: # What `seetrex-verifier <subcommand> --help` REALLY exits with, in this tree.
# This file is an OBSERVATION, not a claim. `crates/verifier/tests/bin_e2e.rs`
# spawns the built executable once per row and asserts the row against the
# process's real exit code, and asserts that the rows are exactly the
# subcommands the binary's own `--help` lists. A subcommand cannot land, and an
# exit code cannot change, without this file moving with it.
# `crates/witness/tests/kit_doc.rs` reads this file INSTEAD OF PARSING the
# verifier's source. Three source-text matchers were defeated in three
# consecutive rounds: a character window reached the neighbouring match arm;
# brace matching from the nearest preceding `=> {` was beaten by a nested
# `match` inside the arm, by a braceless arm above the reject arm, and by a
# `#[cfg]`-gated arm pair. Arm order, nesting and conditional compilation are
# SEMANTICS. No matcher over the text decides them, and each narrower matcher
# shipped a docstring asserting it did.
# Format: <key><TAB><exit code>. Every key is a subcommand and its value the
# exit code of `<subcommand> --help`, EXCEPT the literal `--help`, which is the
# tool's own top-level help: docs/AUDITOR_KIT.md section 7.4(e) publishes that
# code too, and a number an auditor is handed comes from this file or from
# nowhere.
# That last sentence is about THIS file only, and it does not generalise to the
# other record: crates/witness/tests/fixtures/published_verifier_help.tsv, the
# vendored description of the PUBLISHED tool, covers `<subcommand> --help` only
# and carries no `--help` row — one there is refused by name, because every
# non-`version` key in that file is taken for a subcommand.
# Measured in this tree by bin_e2e, which spawns the built executable once per
# row. All six rows were also re-observed 2026-09-01 against the PUBLISHED
# seetrex-verifier 0.3.7, installed from crates.io into an empty root
# (`cargo install seetrex-verifier --locked --version 0.3.7`): every value
# below is identical in the published tool and in this tree, the `--help` row
# included. That closes the re-observation the previous revision of this note
# declared owed — that revision could not make it, because 0.3.7 was the act
# it was part of and not yet a fact it could report. The observation before it,
# 2026-08-31 against the published 0.3.6, recorded the same six values, and the
# one before that, 2026-08-29 against the published 0.3.5, recorded them too:
# no subcommand is added, dropped or re-coded across the three, and no `--help`
# exit code has moved since this record was written.
--help
